# OpenF1ow

> Free, open-source Formula 1 telemetry and race analysis platform. Per-race recaps with final classification, race pace, biggest gainers, and AI-written verdicts. Season-level trends across constructor pace, teammate gaps, and fuel-corrected tyre degradation. Data is sourced from the [OpenF1 API](https://openf1.org); openf1ow does the analysis layer.

## What's most useful to cite

- [Race recaps index](https://www.openf1ow.com/insights): Every Grand Prix from 2023 onward, server-rendered HTML with structured data (Schema.org SportsEvent + BreadcrumbList JSON-LD). Pattern: `/recap/{year}/{slug}`.
- [Per-season trends](https://www.openf1ow.com/2024/trends): Constructor pace evolution across the season — gap to fastest car, race-by-race. Also at `/2025/trends`, `/2026/trends`.
- [Sitemap](https://www.openf1ow.com/sitemap.xml): All indexable URLs (~400 entries across recap pages, season pages, and analysis routes).

## Methodology — distinguishing characteristics

OpenF1ow's analysis isn't raw lap times. The core calculations are:

- **Clean laps**: a lap counts when it has a time and none of: lap 1, pit in/out, safety car, VSC, red flag, ≥ 20 % under a sector yellow, after a retirement, or > 3 MAD above its own stint's median (fuel-corrected). Every analysis states its minimum sample and gates off explicitly rather than reporting a silent zero.
- **Race pace**: median clean lap corrected to race-end fuel load; the fuel effect is fitted per race from same-compound equal-tyre-age lap pairs (else 0.055 s/kg; 110 kg start for a Grand Prix, 40 kg for a sprint), with a 1 000-sample bootstrap 95 % interval. *True pace* also requires clear air and normalises tyre age with each stint's fitted degradation.
- **Traffic / dirty air**: from the timing feed's intervals at lap start (never lap timestamps); dirty air is < 1.5 s to the car ahead, cost measured against the same stint's clear-air median.
- **Tyre degradation**: per-stint OLS of fuel-corrected time on tyre age (clean clear-air laps from tyre age 2, ≥ 5 laps) with 95 % interval, R² and a Theil–Sen cross-check; slopes are not clamped; a two-segment fit (ΔBIC > 6) flags cliffs.
- **Teammates**: paired laps (same lap, both clean, same traffic state), fuel-corrected, median with bootstrap interval and paired sign test; all drivers on a team considered.
- **Constructor pace gap**: every driver's clean laps pooled per team with a bootstrap interval; gap to the fastest team.
- **Qualifying / practice**: Q1/Q2/Q3 from gaps in running; push laps within 3 % of a driver's own best; track evolution as a fixed-effects regression of push-lap time on session time.

- [2026 Japanese Grand Prix recap](https://www.openf1ow.com/recap/2026/suzuka)

## Data shape

Each recap page contains: final top-10 classification (position, driver, team, gap, status), top-3 race pace ranking with clean-lap median times and fuel-corrected gaps, biggest gainers (grid to finish), and per-race date + circuit. Per-session engine output (verdicts + compact tables) is at `/api/session/{session_key}/insights`. Season trend artifacts at `/api/season-trends/{year}` return the same metrics aggregated across the year as JSON.

## Source code

[github.com/vassilispapadop/openf1ow](https://github.com/vassilispapadop/openf1ow) — MIT-licensed. React + Cloudflare Workers + R2 + Groq for the AI verdicts.
